record.original_question: Let G be a 3-connected cubic graph with a blue-red vertex coloring. Write B and R for the subgraphs induced by the blue and red vertices. A crumby coloring is one with maximum degree Delta(B) <= 1, minimum degree delta(R) >= 1, and no path with 3 edges in R. Since the original conjecture asserting that every 3-connected cubic graph has such a coloring is false, what relaxation of the conditions imposed on the red induced subgraph R is sufficient to guarantee that every 3-connected cubic graph admits a blue-red coloring of this type?

evidence.quote: Consider a blue-red vertex coloring of a 3-connected cubic graph G. Denote by B and R the subgraphs of G induced on blue and red vertices, respectively. In [2] Thomassen conjectured that there is always such a blue-red coloring of G where Delta(B) <= 1, delta(R) >= 1 and R does not contain a path with 3 edges. Such a coloring is known as a crumby coloring.

However, the conjecture on crumby colorings is false. Hence, the following question arises: Problem 1.1 What relaxation of the conditions on R guarantees that such a coloring of a 3-connected cubic graph always exists?

artifact.status_search_result: The original Thomassen-style crumby coloring conjecture for 3-connected cubic graphs was disproved by Bellitto, Klimošová, Merker, Witkowski and Yuditsky, who constructed an infinite counterexample family. The follow-up question of finding the right relaxation of the conditions on the red subgraph that holds for all 3-connected cubic graphs remains open; partial positive results are known only for restricted classes (e.g., 2-connected outerplanar graphs, subdivisions of K_4, 1-subdivisions of cubic graphs).

status_evidence.title: Crumby colorings — Red-blue vertex partition of subcubic graphs regarding a conjecture of Thomassen
status_evidence.snippet: Crumby colorings of subcubic graphs related to Thomassen's conjecture; partial results for outerplanar graphs and subdivisions.
status_evidence.claim: The crumby coloring conjecture is studied; positive results exist only for special graph classes.

status_evidence.title: Counterexamples to Thomassen's conjecture on decomposition of cubic graphs
status_evidence.snippet: An infinite family of cubic graphs refuting Thomassen's crumby coloring conjecture is constructed.
status_evidence.claim: The original conjecture is false, leaving the relaxation question open.
